the release's own verdict, from the release's own SecTrustEvaluate (SecTrust.h:359-360, __IPHONE_2_0). THE EFFECT IS A REAL DIFFERENCE AND IS STATED: this function's contract is to return the result of an EARLIER evaluation, and 6.1.3 has no stored result to read - SecTrustGetResult is __IPHONE_NA, never on iOS in any release - so the verdict is COMPUTED ON THE CALL. A caller that changed a policy and asked again gets a freshly evaluated answer, where a later release hands back the earlier one
entries.reason: NOT the one-call wrapper the decision table claimed. The header's deprecation message points at SecTrustGetResult and that reads as the release having the call, but its availability line is __OSX_AVAILABLE_BUT_DEPRECATED(__MAC_10_2, __MAC_10_7, __IPHONE_NA, __IPHONE_NA) (SecTrust.h:758-760) - __IPHONE_NA means it has NEVER been on iOS, so a wrapper for it would not link on a 6.1.3 band. What iOS has is the evaluation itself, so the port evaluates

the constant is the string sync, the key of the attribute; an item added with it true or false is kept on this device only, and a query that names it, true, false or Any, finds the items of the device whichever it names
entries.reason: a departure from 7.0 in what the keychain does with it: the keychain of iOS 6 takes the key and ignores it, and there is no iCloud Keychain to carry an item anywhere
